claims.statement: The marabbecca is a legendary creature from Sicily, its name probably of Arabic origin; it lives in wells and reservoirs, looks like a woman or an amphibian and moves only at night.
claims.statement_id: Marabbecca adalah makhluk legendaris dari Sisilia, yang namanya kemungkinan berasal dari bahasa Arab; ia tinggal di sumur dan waduk, berwujud perempuan atau amfibi, dan hanya bergerak pada malam hari.
claims.quote: The marabbecca is a legendary creature that originates from Sicily. The creature, whose name is likely of Arab origin, lives in wells and reservoirs, takes the appearance of a woman or amphibian and only moves at night.

claims.statement: It is thought to have been invented by Sicilian parents to keep children from playing near wells.
claims.statement_id: Ia diduga diciptakan para orang tua Sisilia agar anak-anak tidak bermain dekat sumur.
claims.quote: It is believed to have been invented by Sicilian parents to prevent their children from playing near wells.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, the creature lives in wells and cisterns and was invented by Sicilian mothers to scare children away from the dangers of an open well.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, makhluk ini tinggal di sumur dan bak penampungan dan diciptakan para ibu Sisilia untuk menakuti anak agar menjauhi bahaya sumur terbuka.
claims.quote: Quest'essere (il cui nome ha probabili origini arabe) vive nei pozzi e nelle cisterne ed è stato inventato dalle madri siciliane per spaventare i figli e tenerli lontani dai pericoli che un pozzo scoperto può determinare.

claims.statement: The Macedonian article also says it is of Arabic origin, lives in wells and reservoirs, looks like a woman and moves only at night.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Makedonia juga menyebutnya berasal-usul Arab, tinggal di sumur dan waduk, berwujud perempuan, dan hanya bergerak pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Марабеката е од арапско потекло и живее во бунари и акумулации, има изглед на жена и се движи само ноќе.

claims.statement: Margot the fairy is, in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne, the generic name of certain earthly fairies, best known in central Brittany, especially the Côtes-d'Armor.
claims.statement_id: Margot la fée adalah nama umum untuk sejumlah peri bumi dalam tradisi Bretagne dan Mayenne, paling dikenal di Bretagne Tengah, terutama Côtes-d'Armor.
claims.quote: Margot the fairy is, in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne, the generic name for certain earthly fairies. They are best known in Central Brittany, particularly in the Côtes-d'Armor.

claims.statement: Probably descended from the fairy Morgana and, before her, from an aspect of Mother Earth, the Margot fairies are powerful: they can turn invisible, change shape and transform others.
claims.statement_id: Kemungkinan berasal dari peri Morgana dan sebelumnya dari satu aspek Ibu Bumi, peri Margot sangat kuat: mereka dapat menghilang, berubah wujud, dan mengubah orang lain.
claims.quote: Presumably descended from the fairy Morgana and before her from an aspect of Mother Earth, the Margot fairies are quite powerful. They can make themselves invisible, metamorphose and transform others.

claims.statement: They are fine dancers, often generous and sometimes cruel, who enjoy testing humans with gifts of gold and objects, are believed to have built several monuments and to hide great treasure underground, and keep animals, often cattle.
claims.statement_id: Mereka penari ulung, sering murah hati dan kadang kejam, senang menguji manusia dengan memberi emas dan benda, dipercaya membangun sejumlah monumen, menyimpan harta besar di bawah tanah, dan memelihara hewan, sering ternak.
claims.quote: Reputed to be excellent dancers, often generous and sometimes cruel, they take pleasure in testing humans by giving them gold and objects. They are believed to have built several monuments, and to possess immense treasures hidden under the earth. They have animals, often cattle.

claims.statement: Tales tell how they steal human children, leaving their own in their place, and become godmothers of babies whom they name and endow with more or less useful gifts.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng menceritakan mereka menculik anak manusia dan menggantinya dengan anak mereka sendiri, serta menjadi ibu baptis bayi yang mereka beri nama dan hadiah yang kadang merepotkan.
claims.quote: Tales and myths tell of the habits of these fairies, who kidnap human children to replace them with their own and become the godmothers of babies whom they name and cover with more or less convenient gifts.

claims.statement: They reward the righteous and punish those who harm them or are greedy or indiscreet with them, and sometimes steal.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memberi hadiah kepada orang benar dan menghukum yang menyakiti, serakah, atau lancang terhadap mereka, dan kadang mencuri.
claims.quote: They reward the righteous and punish those who harm them, are greedy or indiscreet towards them. They sometimes show themselves to be thieves.

claims.statement: According to the French article, many megaliths and rocks are said to be these fairies' homes or their furniture and tools: table, spindle, room, clog, armchair, cradle.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, banyak megalit dan batu besar dianggap rumah peri-peri ini atau perabot dan perkakas mereka: meja, alat pintal, kamar, sabot, kursi, dan buaian.
claims.quote: De nombreux mégalithes et rochers seraient les demeures de ces fées, ou bien leurs meubles et leurs outils : table, fuseau, chambre, sabot, fauteuil, berceau…

claims.statement: They were the object of cults, especially at the Margot cave; until the end of the 19th century these beliefs led many people to sacrifice animals to them and hunt for their treasures.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menjadi sasaran pemujaan, terutama di gua Margot; sampai akhir abad ke-19 kepercayaan ini membuat banyak orang mempersembahkan hewan kepada mereka dan mencari harta mereka.
claims.quote: They were the object of cults and beliefs, in particular at the Margot cave. These beliefs, until the end of the 19th century, led many people to offer them animals in sacrifice and to search for their supposed treasures.

claims.statement: The name probably distorts that of Morgana, the famous fairy of Arthurian myth; in Lower Brittany they were first called Morgana.
claims.statement_id: Namanya mungkin pelesetan nama Morgana, peri terkenal mitos Arthur; di Bretagne Bawah mereka semula disebut Morgana.
claims.quote: The name probably comes from a distortion of the name of Morgana, the famous fairy of the Arthurian myth. They were originally called "Morgana" in Lower Brittany.

claims.statement: Roger Sherman Loomis sees a link between the fairies of Upper Brittany and the Morgain of the Arthurian romances.
claims.statement_id: Roger Sherman Loomis melihat hubungan antara peri Bretagne Atas dan Morgain dalam roman Arthur.
claims.quote: Roger Sherman Loomis sees a relationship between the fairies of Upper Brittany and the "Morgain" of the Arthurian romances.

claims.statement: The Spanish article also calls Margot the fairy the generic name of certain earthly fairies in the traditions of Brittany and the Mayenne.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut peri Margot nama umum sejumlah peri bumi dalam tradisi Bretagne dan Mayenne.
claims.quote: El hada Margot (en francés, Margot la fée) es, en las tradiciones de Bretaña y Mayenne, el nombre genérico de algunas hadas terrestres.

claims.statement: Ahari or Aari is a 'ram' in Basque mythology, one of Mari's subordinate night spirits.
claims.statement_id: Ahari atau Aari adalah "domba jantan" dalam mitologi Basque, salah satu roh malam bawahan Mari.
claims.quote: Ahari ou Aari est un « bélier » dans la mythologie basque et un des génies nocturnes subalternes de Mari.

claims.statement: Ahari means 'ram' in Basque.
claims.statement_id: Ahari berarti "domba jantan" dalam bahasa Basque.
claims.quote: Ahari signifie « bélier » en basque.

claims.statement: According to the Catalan article, Ahari is one of the ireluak, Basque night spirits, which sometimes appears as a woman or child, sometimes as an animal, and lives in the Okina cave at Bernedo (Alava) as a ram.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Katalan, Ahari adalah salah satu irelu, roh malam Basque, yang kadang muncul sebagai perempuan atau anak, kadang sebagai hewan, dan tinggal di gua Okina di Bernedo (Alava) dalam wujud domba jantan.
claims.quote: Ahari és un dels ireluak, genis nocturns de la mitologia basca, que de vegades s'apareix com una dona o un nen, de vegades com un animal, i que viu a la famosa cova d'Okina, a Bernedo (Àlaba), en forma de marrà.

claims.statement: The irelu rams living in caves are generally Mari's servants; the goddess uses their bodies as pillows and their horns as distaffs.
claims.statement_id: Domba jantan irelu yang tinggal di gua umumnya pelayan Mari; sang dewi memakai tubuhnya sebagai bantal tidur dan tanduknya sebagai alat pintal.
claims.quote: Generalment, els marrans "irelu" que viuen a les coves són servents de Mari. La deessa en fa servir el cos de coixí per a dormir i les banyes de filosa.

claims.statement: Sometimes, leaving her cave, Mari rides the rams like horses, as in the case of the Lady of Aketegi, one of Mari's names, at Zegama.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ketika keluar dari gua Mari menunggangi domba jantan seperti kuda, misalnya dalam kisah Dama d'Aketegi, salah satu nama Mari, di Zegama.
claims.quote: De vegades, quan surt de la cova, Mari fa servir els marrans de muntura, cavalcant-hi com si anés a cavall. Aquesta creença, per exemple, s'aplica al cas de la Dama d'Aketegi (un dels molts noms de Mari), a Zegama.

claims.statement: The ram (ahari, with dialect forms aari, adari, ari) is a very common animal in Basque mythology.
claims.statement_id: Domba jantan (ahari, dengan varian dialek aari, adari, ari) adalah hewan yang sangat umum dalam mitologi Basque.
claims.quote: El marrà (en basc: ahari, amb les variants dialectals aari, adari, ari i altres) és un animal molt habitual en la mitologia basca

claims.statement: Basque rural sports (herri kirolak) include ram fighting (ahari topeka).
claims.statement_id: Dalam olahraga pedesaan Basque (herri kirolak) ada adu domba jantan (ahari topeka).
claims.quote: Dans les sports ruraux ou herri kirolak, parmi les nombreuses épreuves pastorales, on trouve le combat de béliers (ahari topeka)

claims.statement: The Basque article also says Ahari is the name of an irelu said to live in the famous Okina cave in Alava, taking the form of a ram.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Basque juga menyebut Ahari nama irelu yang konon tinggal di gua Okina di Alava dan berwujud domba jantan.
claims.quote: Ahari Arabako Okinako leize ospetsuan bizi omen zen ireluetako baten izena da, ahariaren itxura hartzen zuena.

claims.statement: Matlalcueitl is the goddess of rain and songs in Tlaxcala mythology, who gave her name to a volcano better known as La Malinche.
claims.statement_id: Matlalcueitl adalah dewi hujan dan nyanyian dalam mitologi Tlaxcala, yang memberi nama pada gunung api yang lebih dikenal sebagai La Malinche.
claims.quote: Matlalcueitl est la déesse de la pluie et des chansons dans la mythologie Tlaxcala. Elle a donné son nom à un volcan plus communément appelé La Malinche.

claims.statement: According to the Tlaxcalans, Matlalcueye is the goddess of rain and earthly waters, consort of Tlaloc the rain god; she was also known as Chalchiuhtlicue.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang Tlaxcala, Matlalcueye adalah dewi hujan dan air di bumi, permaisuri Tlaloc sang dewa hujan; ia juga dikenal sebagai Chalchiuhtlicue.
claims.quote: es la Diosa de la lluvia y las aguas terrestres, consorte de Tlaloc, Dios de la lluvia, según los tlaxcaltecas. También fue conocida como Chalchiuhtlicue.

claims.statement: Her name literally means 'she of the blue skirt', from the mountain's colour and long slopes; her other name, Chalchiuhtlicue, means 'her skirt of jade'.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "yang berrok biru", sesuai warna dan lereng panjang gunungnya; nama lainnya, Chalchiuhtlicue, berarti "roknya dari giok".
claims.quote: Su nombre quiere decir textualmente "la de la falda azul", por su color evidente y sus laderas largas. Su otro nombre, Chalchiuhtlicue, quiere decir "su falda (de) jade".

claims.statement: After Xochiquetzal she is Tlaloc's second wife: Malintzin, the mountain from whose skirts rivers truly flow.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Xochiquetzal, ia istri kedua Tlaloc: Malintzin, gunung yang dari kakinya memang mengalir sungai-sungai.
claims.quote: Después de Xochiquetzal , es la segunda esposa de Tláloc: Malintzin, montaña de cuya falda efectivamente brotan ríos.

claims.statement: Like other rain-giving mountains she was also called Coatlicue ('she of the serpent skirt'), since clouds were likened to snakes and cloud serpents (mixkoatl) were said to be born on the mountain.
claims.statement_id: Seperti gunung pemberi hujan lain, ia juga disebut Coatlicue ("yang berrok ular"), karena awan diumpamakan ular dan ular awan (mixkoatl) dikatakan lahir di gunung itu.
claims.quote: También como otras montañas dadoras de lluvia, era llamada Coatlicue (la de la falda de víboras) pues las nubes eran comparadas con serpientes y decían que las serpientes de nubes (mixkoatl) nacían en la montaña

claims.statement: In the Yumhu (Otomi) language she is Mhu Ye, 'Rain Goddess', and like the Nahuatl-speaking peoples they depict her as half woman, half snake, appearing so to the people of Tlaxcala.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Yumhu (Otomi) ia disebut Mhu Ye, "Dewi Hujan", dan seperti bangsa berbahasa Nahuatl mereka menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan setengah manusia setengah ular yang menampakkan diri kepada penduduk Tlaxcala.
claims.quote: En lengua yumhu se llama Mhu Ye (Diosa de la lluvia) y como los pueblos nahuahablantes, la representan como una mujer mitad humana y mitad culebra y se narra que se aparece de esa forma a los pobladores tlaxcaltecas.

claims.statement: The Italian article calls Matlalcueitl or Matlalcueyetl, 'she who wears a blue skirt', a life-giving goddess of rain and song in Tlaxcala mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia menyebut Matlalcueitl atau Matlalcueyetl, "yang memakai rok biru", dewi hujan pemberi kehidupan dan nyanyian dalam mitologi Tlaxcala.
claims.quote: Matlalcueitl o Matlalcueyetl o Matlalcueje (in lingua náhuatl Matlaltic-Cueitl ovvero [Colei che Indossa una] Gonna Azzurra) è una divinità della pioggia donatrice di vita e della canzone, nella mitologia di Tlaxcala.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology she was identified with Chalchiuhtlicue, consort of the ancient rain god Tlaloc.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztek ia disamakan dengan Chalchiuhtlicue, permaisuri dewa hujan kuno Tlaloc.
claims.quote: Nella mitologia azteca veniva identificata con Chalchiuhtlicue e con il consorte, l'antico dio della pioggia Tlaloc.

claims.statement: The mazapégul, known by several other Romagnol names, are mischievous night elves of the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì in northern Italy.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul, yang punya banyak nama lain dalam bahasa Romagnol, adalah peri malam yang usil dalam cerita rakyat Romagna, terutama di Pegunungan Apennine sekitar Forlì, Italia utara.
claims.quote: The mazapégul, also known by several other names in Romagnol, are mischievous nocturnal elves in the folklore of Romagna, especially around the Apennines of Forlì, in northern Italy.

claims.statement: They are shown as a cross between apes and homunculi with grey fur, also like cats or monkeys, wearing a distinctive red cap they need for their mischief.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai campuran kera dan manusia kecil berbulu kelabu, mirip kucing atau monyet, dan memakai topi merah khas yang mereka perlukan untuk berbuat usil.
claims.quote: The elves are portrayed as a cross between apes and homunculi, with grey fur, also resembling cats or monkeys. They wear a distinctive red cap, which they require to perform their mischief.

claims.statement: The mazapégul are blamed for nightmares, including sleep paralysis and choking sensations, tousling sleeping women's hair, stomach aches, vanishing objects, clashing cymbals and flying dishes.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul dianggap menyebabkan mimpi buruk, termasuk kelumpuhan tidur dan rasa tercekik, mengacak rambut perempuan yang tidur, sakit perut, menghilangkan benda, memainkan simbal, dan membuat piring beterbangan.
claims.quote: The mazapégul are credited for causing nightmares, including sleep paralysis or sensations of suffocation, ruffling women's hair in their sleep, causing stomach pains, making objects disappear, playing the cymbals, causing dishes to fly, and making victims gain weight.

claims.statement: In the countryside they bother animals, especially horses, which wake sweating with braided tails and manes.
claims.statement_id: Di pedesaan mereka mengganggu hewan, terutama kuda, yang bangun pagi dengan tubuh berkeringat serta ekor dan surai terkepang.
claims.quote: In the countryside, they disturb animals, especially horses, who wake in the mornings covered in sweat and with braided tails and manes.

claims.statement: Drawn to pretty girls, they enter their rooms at night, fall asleep on their stomachs and praise them: 'What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!'
claims.statement_id: Tertarik pada gadis cantik, mereka masuk ke kamar gadis pada malam hari, tidur di atas perutnya, dan memujinya: "Betapa indah matamu! Betapa indah rambutmu!"
claims.quote: Attracted by beautiful young girls, the elves enter their rooms at night and fall asleep on their stomachs. They compliment them, saying: "What beautiful eyes! What beautiful hair!"

claims.statement: If its cap is stolen or thrown down the well, the thief may be pestered at night with the cry 'give me back my cap!'
claims.statement_id: Bila topinya dicuri atau dilempar ke sumur, si pencuri bisa diganggu setiap malam dengan tuntutan "kembalikan topiku!".
claims.quote: If its cap is stolen or thrown into the well, either its vanquisher is tormented at night with the demand of "give me back my cap!"

claims.statement: Grains of rice scattered on a windowsill keep the mazapégul busy counting them until daybreak.
claims.statement_id: Menaburkan butir beras di ambang jendela membuat mazapégul sibuk menghitungnya sampai fajar.
claims.quote: sprinkling grains of rice on a windowsill so that the mazapégul is distracted by counting them until daybreak.

claims.statement: The mazapégul descend from the incubus, a demon that troubled sleepers and preyed on women, and share traits with elves elsewhere, such as the Laurieddhu of southern Italy and those of the French Vosges.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul diturunkan dari inkubus, iblis yang mengganggu orang tidur dan memperdaya perempuan, dan memiliki kemiripan dengan peri daerah lain seperti Laurieddhu dari Italia selatan dan peri Vosges di Prancis.
claims.quote: The mazapégul  descend from the mythological incubus, a demon that would disturb sleeping humans and take advantage of women. They share characteristics with elves from other regions of Italy, such as the Laurieddhu ... of southern Italy, as well as from the French Vosges.

claims.statement: Mazapégul lore is recorded in Giuliano Fantaguzzi's survey of early 15th-century Cesena.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat tentang mazapégul tercatat dalam tinjauan Giuliano Fantaguzzi tentang Cesena awal abad ke-15.
claims.quote: Folklore surrounding the mazapégul is recorded in a survey of early 15th-century Cesena by Giuliano Fantaguzzi.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the family name is first recorded in an extract of a sales contract of 9 May 1487 in the General Archive of Forlì.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, nama keluarga peri ini pertama kali tercatat dalam kutipan kontrak jual beli tertanggal 9 Mei 1487 di Arsip Umum Forlì.
claims.quote: El nombre de la familia que se menciona está documentado por primera vez en un extracto de un contrato de venta del 9 de mayo de 1487 en el Archivo general de Forlì

claims.statement: The Italian article also calls the Mazapégul a sprite (folletto) of the folk tradition of Romagna, especially the Forlì Apennines.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia juga menyebut Mazapégul peri usil (folletto) dari tradisi rakyat Romagna, terutama Apennine Forlì.
claims.quote: Il Mazapégul è un folletto della mitologia italiana, appartenente alla tradizione folclorica della Romagna, in particolare dell'Appennino forlivese.

claims.statement: The mazapégul, especially its red cap, appears in Romagnol carnival costumes.
claims.statement_id: Mazapégul, terutama topi merahnya, muncul dalam kostum karnaval Romagna.
claims.quote: The mazapégul, particularly its red cap, features in Romagnol carnival costumes.

claims.statement: Mikelats is a figure of Basque mythology who makes storms and hurls stones, with powers like the Scandinavian god Thor.
claims.statement_id: Mikelats adalah tokoh mitologi Basque yang menciptakan badai dan melemparkan batu, dengan kekuatan mirip dewa Thor dari mitologi Skandinavia.
claims.quote: Mikelats (prononcer « mikélatche ») est un personnage de la mythologie basque, il crée les orages et projette des pierres. Il a des pouvoirs similaires au dieu Thor de la mythologie scandinave.

claims.statement: Mikelats is the child of Mari and Maju; farmers see him as evil, and by legend he and his mother make storms and hurl them at herds and harvests to punish people who did not respect their mother.
claims.statement_id: Mikelats adalah anak Mari dan Maju; para petani menganggapnya jahat, dan menurut legenda bersama ibunya ia menciptakan badai dan melemparkannya ke ternak dan panen untuk menghukum manusia yang tidak menghormati ibu mereka.
claims.quote: Mikelats est l'enfant de Mari et Maju. Les paysans le voient comme une créature maléfique. Selon une légende, Avec sa mère Mari, il crée des tempêtes et les lance contre le troupeau et la moisson, pour punir les humains qui ne respectaient pas leur mère.

claims.statement: According to the Catalan article, he is one of the two sons of Mari and Sugaar and personifies evil, while his elder brother Atarrabi embodies good.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Katalan, ia salah satu dari dua putra Mari dan Sugaar yang mempersonifikasikan kejahatan, sedangkan kakaknya Atarrabi mewujudkan kebaikan.
claims.quote: Mikelats és un personatge destacat de la mitologia basca. És un dels dos fills de Mari (la deessa suprema basca) i Sugaar i representa la personificació del mal, mentre que el seu germà gran, Atarrabi, encarna el bé.

claims.statement: In some legends he appears as Hodei or Odei ('cloud'), and scholars see him as evil personified because he can strike fields and orchards with hail through storms.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian legenda ia muncul sebagai Hodei atau Odei ("awan"), dan para peneliti menganggapnya personifikasi kejahatan karena dapat menghantam ladang dan kebun dengan hujan es lewat badai.
claims.quote: Mikelats, que també apareix com a Hodei o Odei ('núvol') en algunes llegendes, és considerat per tots els estudiosos com la personificació del mal, ja que posseeix el poder de colpejar camps i horts amb calamarsa per mitjà de tempestes

claims.statement: His name joins Mikel (Michael, the archangel who defeated Lucifer) and hats ('breath').
claims.statement_id: Namanya terdiri dari Mikel (Mikael, nama malaikat agung pengalah Lucifer) dan hats ("napas").
claims.quote: El seu nom ja és prou indicatiu, car està format per Mikel (Miquel, el nom de l'arcàngel principal, vencedor de Llucifer) i hats ('alè').

claims.statement: According to the Basque article, he studied with his brother in the devil's cave on condition that, when they finished, one of them must stay in that dark place.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Basque, ia belajar bersama kakaknya di gua iblis, dengan syarat setelah selesai salah satu dari mereka harus tinggal di tempat gelap itu.
claims.quote: Bere anaiarekin batera deabruaren haitzuloan ikasi zuen, bertan kultura zabala erakutsi zieten. Baina baldintza bat zegoen: ikasketak amaitu ondoren, bietako bat leku ilun hartan geratu beharko zen.

claims.statement: The lot fell on Mikelats to stay, but big-hearted Atarrabi chose at the last moment to remain as a servant, so Mikelats went out free.
claims.statement_id: Undian menetapkan Mikelats harus tinggal, tetapi Atarrabi yang berhati besar memilih tinggal sebagai pelayan di saat terakhir, sehingga Mikelats keluar dan bebas.
claims.quote: Garaia iritsitakoan, han geratu behar zena Mikelats izatea erabaki zuen zoriak, baina bere anaiak, Atarrabik, hain zuen bihotz handia, azken unean morroi bezala geratzea erabaki zuela, honela, Mikelats irten eta aske izan zen.

claims.statement: Both attended the school the devil, called Etsai in the legends, ran in a dark cave, where they gained wide learning.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya bersekolah di gua gelap yang dikelola iblis, yang dalam legenda disebut Etsai, dan memperoleh pengetahuan luas.
claims.quote: Tots dos van anar a l'escola que el diable, anomenat a les llegendes Etsai, regentava en una fosca cova, on van adquirir una vasta cultura.

claims.statement: Barandiaran wrote that he did not dwell on irelu such as Eate, Odei and Mikelats because the stories about them shift between different figures.
claims.statement_id: Barandiaran menulis bahwa ia tidak membahas khusus irelu seperti Eate, Odei, dan Mikelats karena kisah-kisah tentang mereka berpindah-pindah di antara berbagai tokoh.
claims.quote: Selon Barandiaran : « Nous ne nous sommes pas arrêtés, par exemple, à considérer certains Irelu, comme ces derniers Eate, Odei et Mikelats, car une grande partie des sujets qui s'y réfèrent changent entre certains personnages et d'autres

issues.message: Di bawah target core: 5 klaim (target 6). gaps sudah diisi; nilai apakah pencariannya memadai.

claims.statement: Mirokutana is a night spirit of Basque mythology that looks like a wolf or a dog, known around Oiartzun and said to live in the Peñas de Aya massif.
claims.statement_id: Mirokutana adalah roh malam mitologi Basque yang berwujud serigala atau anjing, dikenal di daerah Oiartzun dan konon tinggal di pegunungan Peñas de Aya.
claims.quote: Mirokutana és un geni nocturn de la mitologia basca que adopta l'aparença de llop o de gos. És conegut a la zona d'Oiartzun i es diu que viu a la zona del massís de les Peñas de Aya.

claims.statement: The Basque article also calls it a mythical being shaped like a wolf or dog that roams at night and is known around Oiartzun.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Basque juga menyebutnya makhluk mitologi berwujud serigala atau anjing yang berkeliaran pada malam hari dan dikenal di sekitar Oiartzun.
claims.quote: Mirokutana otso ala txakur itxura daukan mitologiako izakia da. Gauetan ibiltzen da eta Oiartzun aldean da ezaguna.

claims.statement: It belongs to the group of irelu in Basque mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ia termasuk golongan irelu dalam mitologi Basque.
claims.quote: Mirokutana euskal mitologian agertzen diren ireluen multzoan sartzen da.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra and Mirokutana are Basque spirits shaped like dogs, whose powers differ by place and legend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra, dan Mirokutana adalah roh Basque berwujud anjing yang kekuatannya berbeda menurut tempat dan legendanya.
claims.quote: Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra et Mirokutana sont des génies de la mythologie basque qui ont l'aspect d'un chien. Outre le fait d'apparaitre comme des chiens, leurs pouvoirs diffèrent selon les lieux et les légendes.

claims.statement: Through syncretism with Christianity, dogs were often taken to be possessed by the spirits of those who died unconfessed.
claims.statement_id: Lewat sinkretisme dengan agama Kristen, anjing sering dianggap makhluk yang dirasuki roh orang yang mati tanpa pengakuan dosa.
claims.quote: C'est pourquoi, à partir du syncrétisme qui a généré la nouvelle religion, à de nombreuses reprises, les chiens sont pris pour des êtres possédés par les esprits de ceux qui sont morts sans confession

claims.statement: The Monster of Lake Fagua is a legendary creature claimed to have been found in a lake near Santa Fe, Chile; a 1784 article in the Courier de L'Europe in France said it had been caught and would be shown in Europe.
claims.statement_id: Monster Danau Fagua adalah makhluk legendaris yang diklaim ditemukan di danau dekat Santa Fe, Chili; sebuah artikel di Courier de L'Europe di Prancis tahun 1784 menyebutnya telah ditangkap dan akan dipamerkan di Eropa.
claims.quote: The Monster of Lake Fagua is a legendary creature, which it was claimed had been found in a lake near a place called Santa Fe, in Chile. An article about the creature was written in the Courier de L'Europe in France in 1784 stating that it had been captured and was going to be on display in Europe.

claims.statement: The creature is described as 20 feet (6.1 m) long, with a human face, bull-like horns, huge donkey ears, lion's teeth, bat wings, and a dragon's lower body with two long pointed tails for stinging enemies.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu digambarkan sepanjang 20 kaki (6,1 m), berwajah manusia, bertanduk seperti banteng, bertelinga keledai besar, bergigi singa, bersayap kelelawar, dan bertubuh bawah naga dengan dua ekor panjang runcing untuk menyengat musuh.
claims.quote: The creature is described as being 20 feet (6.1 m) long, with a human face, bull-like horns, huge donkey-like ears, lion-like teeth, bat-like wings, and the lower body of a dragon with two long pointed tails which it used to sting and attack enemies.

claims.statement: It was said to be nocturnal and to eat livestock such as cattle and pigs.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon aktif pada malam hari dan memakan ternak seperti sapi dan babi.
claims.quote: It was said to be nocturnal and its diet consisted of livestock, like cattle and pigs.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the monster of Lake Fagua is an imaginary lake creature presented as real in several prints sold in Paris in October 1784.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, monster danau Fagua adalah makhluk danau khayalan yang disajikan sebagai nyata dalam beberapa cetakan gambar yang dijual di Paris pada Oktober 1784.
claims.quote: Le monstre du lac Fagua est une créature lacustre imaginaire, présentée comme réelle sur plusieurs estampes vendues à Paris en octobre 1784.

claims.statement: The craze for this 'harpy' was such that it inspired new fancies among fashionable ladies' hairdressers.
claims.statement_id: Kegemaran pada "harpy" ini begitu besar sehingga mengilhami gaya rambut baru para perempuan modis.
claims.quote: L'engouement pour cette « harpie » est tel qu'il inspire de nouvelles fantaisies aux coiffeurs des élégantes, qui appréciaient alors les coiffures extravagantes.

claims.statement: The Japanese article notes that 'Lake Fagua' does not exist and is an invented place name, so the creature report is equally doubtful.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jepang mencatat bahwa "Danau Fagua" tidak ada dan merupakan nama tempat rekaan, sehingga laporan tentang makhluk itu juga meragukan.
claims.quote: ところが、この説明に登場する「ファグア湖」は実在せず、架空の地名であるため、生物の報告も同様に疑わしい。

claims.statement: Annie Duprat interpreted it as a caricature of Marie Antoinette.
claims.statement_id: Annie Duprat menafsirkannya sebagai karikatur Marie Antoinette.
claims.quote: アニー・デュプラはこれをマリー・アントワネットの風刺画であると解釈した。

claims.statement: The Monster of Ravenna was a possibly apocryphal monstrous birth of the late Renaissance whose appearance near Ravenna in early 1512 was widely reported in European pamphlets and diaries of the time.
claims.statement_id: Monster Ravenna adalah kelahiran aneh dari akhir masa Renaisans, mungkin apokrif, yang kemunculannya di dekat Ravenna awal 1512 banyak dilaporkan dalam pamflet dan catatan harian Eropa masa itu.
claims.quote: The Monster of Ravenna was a possibly apocryphal late Renaissance-era monstrous birth whose appearance in early 1512 near the city of Ravenna was widely reported in contemporary European pamphlets and diaries.

claims.statement: Its grotesque features were read symbolically by opponents of both the Catholic Church and the Protestant Reformation, though the commoner explanation then was that it was an omen of the Battle of Ravenna (1512).
claims.statement_id: Gambaran rupanya yang aneh ditafsirkan secara simbolis oleh penentang Gereja Katolik maupun Reformasi Protestan, tetapi penjelasan yang lebih umum saat itu ialah bahwa makhluk itu pertanda hasil Pertempuran Ravenna (1512).
claims.quote: Images of its grotesque features were interpreted symbolically by opponents of both the Catholic Church and the Protestant Reformation, although a more common explanation at the time was that the beast was an omen regarding the outcome of the Battle of Ravenna (1512).

claims.statement: Modern medical consensus identifies the monster as a child with a severe congenital disorder.
claims.statement_id: Konsensus medis modern mengenalinya sebagai anak dengan kelainan bawaan berat.
claims.quote: Modern medical consensus identifies the monster as a child with some variety of severe congenital disorder.

claims.statement: According to the diary of Sebastiano di Branca Tedallini, the child was said to be born of a nun and a friar, with a horned head, the letters YXV on its chest, one hairy cloven-hoofed leg and a human eye in the middle of the other.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan harian Sebastiano di Branca Tedallini, anak itu konon lahir dari seorang biarawati dan biarawan, berkepala bertanduk, bertanda huruf YXV di dadanya, dengan satu kaki berbulu berkuku belah dan kaki lain bermata manusia di tengahnya.
claims.quote: According to his account, the child was said to have been born of a nun and a friar, and was marked by a horned head, the letters YXV on its chest, and with one leg hairy and cloven-hoofed while the other leg's midsection grew a human eye.

claims.statement: Luca Landucci described a single horn, bat wings, hermaphrodite genitals, an eye on the right knee and a clawed left foot like an eagle's.
claims.statement_id: Luca Landucci menggambarkannya bertanduk satu, bersayap kelelawar, berkelamin ganda, bermata di lutut kanan, dan berkaki kiri bercakar seperti elang.
claims.quote: Landucci described it to possess features such as a single horn, the wings of a bat, hermaphroditic genitalia, an eye on its right knee and a clawed left foot like an eagle's.

claims.statement: In medieval Europe malformed infants with little chance of survival were commonly left to starve, and in Ravenna this was done on the Pope's order.
claims.statement_id: Di Eropa abad pertengahan bayi cacat yang kecil peluang hidupnya biasa ditelantarkan hingga mati kelaparan, dan di Ravenna hal ini dilakukan atas perintah Paus.
claims.quote: In medieval Europe, it was common practice for malformed infants, especially those with little chance of survival, to be abandoned and left to die by starvation; this was done in Ravenna on the order of the Pope.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the monster was born in 1511 according to Lycosthenes, the year before the battle, or on the very day (11 April 1512) according to Boaistuau.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, monster itu lahir pada 1511 menurut Lycosthenes, setahun sebelum pertempuran, atau pada hari pertempuran itu sendiri (11 April 1512) menurut Boaistuau.
claims.quote: Le monstre serait né en 1511 à Ravenne, selon Lycosthènes, année précédant la bataille, ou le jour même (11 avril 1512), selon Boaistuau.

claims.statement: The signs on its chest were read as an upsilon (Υ), the desire for virtue, and a cross below it, Christ's teaching, which the Italians failed to follow.
claims.statement_id: Tanda di dadanya ditafsirkan sebagai upsilon (Υ), lambang keinginan akan kebajikan, dan salib di bawahnya ajaran Kristus, yang tidak diikuti orang Italia.
claims.quote: Les Italiens n'ont pas suivi les signes inscrits sur la poitrine du monstre : l'upsilon (Υ) signifiant désir de vertu, et la croix au-dessous l'enseignement du Christ.

claims.statement: The Macedonian article likewise says modern medical consensus identifies it as a child with severe congenital disorders.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Makedonia juga menyebut konsensus medis modern mengenalinya sebagai anak dengan kelainan bawaan berat.
claims.quote: Современиот медицински консензус го идентификувал чудовиштето како дете со различни тешки вродени нарушувања.

claims.statement: The muscaliet is an animal of Medieval bestiaries; Pierre de Beauvais's 13th-century Bestiaire describes it by comparing it in various ways to hares, squirrels, weasels, moles and pigs.
claims.statement_id: Muscaliet adalah hewan dari bestiari Abad Pertengahan; Bestiaire karya Pierre de Beauvais abad ke-13 menggambarkannya dengan membandingkan bagian-bagiannya dengan kelinci, tupai, musang, tikus tanah, dan babi.
claims.quote: The muscaliet is an animal from Medieval bestiaries. Pierre de Beauvais ... 13th century Bestiaire includes a description of the animal, comparing it in various aspects to hares, squirrels, weasels, moles and pigs.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Pierre de Beauvais's 12th-century Bestiaire describes it with a hare's body but smaller, a squirrel's legs and tail, a weasel's ears, a mole's snout, a boar's teeth and a pig's bristly skin.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Bestiaire Pierre de Beauvais dari abad ke-12 menggambarkannya bertubuh kelinci yang lebih kecil, berkaki dan berekor tupai, bertelinga musang, bermoncong tikus tanah, bergigi babi hutan, dan berkulit lebat seperti babi.
claims.quote: Le Bestiaire de Pierre de Beauvais, datant du XIIe siècle, comprend une description de l'animal qui a le corps d'un lièvre (mais plus petit), les pattes et la queue d'un écureuil, les oreilles d'une belette et le museau d'une taupe. Il a des dents de sanglier et sa peau est touffue comme celle d'un porc.

claims.statement: It climbs trees and leaps from branch to branch with its tail, destroys leaves and fruit, nests under the roots, and its natural heat dries the tree until it dies.
claims.statement_id: Ia memanjat pohon, melompat antardahan dengan bantuan ekornya, merusak daun dan buah, bersarang di bawah akar, dan panas tubuhnya membuat pohon kering lalu mati.
claims.quote: Il grimpe aux arbres et saute de branche en branche à l'aide de sa queue. Lorsqu'il grimpe dans un arbre, la muscaliet détruit le feuillage et les fruits. Sous les racines d'un arbre, il fait son nid. Sa chaleur naturelle fait que l'arbre se dessèche et meurt

claims.statement: In Beauvais's moral reading the tree is a person and the muscaliet is Pride, its sharp teeth the cutting words of Cruelty, its feet showing cruelty's persistence.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tafsiran moral Beauvais, pohon adalah manusia dan muscaliet adalah Kesombongan, giginya kata-kata tajam Kekejaman, dan kakinya menunjukkan kekejaman yang gigih.
claims.quote: Mais le muscaliet est l'Orgueil, ses dents acérées sont les mots tranchants qu'apporte la Cruauté, et ses pieds montrent que la cruauté est tenace.

claims.statement: The -caliet may come from Latin calor, 'heat', chosen for a naturally hot creature.
claims.statement_id: Bagian -caliet mungkin berasal dari bahasa Latin calor, "panas", untuk menggambarkan makhluk yang panas secara alami.
claims.quote: Peut-être que le -caliet vient du latin calor et a été choisi pour décrire une créature chaude par nature.

claims.statement: The Dutch article calls the muscaliet a fruit-eating fabulous animal with a smaller hare's body, a squirrel's legs and tail, a weasel's ears and a mole's snout.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Belanda menyebut muscaliet hewan dongeng pemakan buah bertubuh kelinci yang lebih kecil, berkaki dan berekor tupai, bertelinga musang, dan bermoncong tikus tanah.
claims.quote: Een muscaliet is een fruitetend fabeldier dat het lichaam heeft van een haas (maar dan kleiner), de benen en de staart van een eekhoorn, de oren van een wezel en de snuit van een mol.
